messages:
kevin: Heads up — after the 4-bit rollforward this morning we're seeing p50 p95 regressions on the nf4+fp4 combo in eu-west-2. Memory on a subset of inference hosts spiked ~22% and the scheduler started evicting KV shards. :sos:

kevin: quick snapshot from the canary cluster:
```
host: gpu-rt-23
model: gpt-xl-nf4-fp4:v2
seq_len: 1024
throughput_before: 420 req/s
throughput_after: 290 req/s
kv_mem_before: 6.1GB
kv_mem_after: 7.5GB
kernel_selected: 4b_mixed_fastpath_v3 -> fallback to slowpath after 30s
trace: kernel_switch_count=12, batch_fill_rate_drop=0.35
```

maria: @kevin thanks — do we have perf counters showing cache hit rate? sounds like KV fragmentation or an allocator behavior change during the new kernel's slowpath. :thinking_face:

alex: I pushed a tiny telemetry patch earlier to log slab usage per-alloc class. Can you confirm the host id so I can pull logs?

kevin: gpu-rt-23 is the one with visible thrash. there are ~6 hosts showing smaller spikes. attaching tracer output (snippet):
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kv_cache_hits: 1.2M
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kv_cache_misses: 430k
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kv_alloc_frag_ratio: 0.27 -> 0.62
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kernel_fastpath_ms: 1.7 -> 4.9
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kernel_switches: 12
```

maria: frag_ratio jump is huge. that explains the extra memory and slower per-token kernel times. suspect allocator change in the 4b kernel (v3) — maybe new workspace sizing for per-key storage.

alex: on it. hypothesis: the mix of NF4 quant with FP4 fallback paths increases ephemeral KV allocations during beam/kp ops, causing fragmentation. short-term mitigation: pin kernel to v2 for nf4 models on the affected pool and throttle rollforward.

kevin: agreed. can we pin via routing rules? we'd like minimal customer impact (no model downgrade).

infra-bot: DeploymentPlan(nf4-pinning): created rollout -> target_pool=eu-west-2-infer, action=pin_kernel:v2, scope=host_tags=[gpu-rt-*], initiated_by=alex

alex: pinning rolled out to 6 hosts. monitoring now.

maria: next steps for the runtime/rls team: 1) repro with synthetic traffic and worst-case seq_len distribution, 2) run heap profiler to find allocator hot paths, 3) instrument kernel v3 to avoid per-request ephemeral arena allocations. I'll own #1 and #2.

kevin: I'll run the synthetic job with our canonical prompt set and push traces to the perf bucket. also want a baseline microbenchmark for kernel v2 vs v3 (single-token latency + kv growth).

alex: quick checklist — if pin fixes immediate evictions: keep pinned, iterate v3 with allocator changes; if not fixed, rollback v3 completely and gate it behind a canary with stricter batch heuristics.

sre-oncall: FYI we saw 4 customer error spikes on the same hosts (rate-limited 503s) but no broad outage. Keeping page open until kv evictions stop. :eyes:

kevin: i'm seeing p50 recover ~10% after pinning, p95 still elevated. will share new traces in ~15m.

maria: thanks. once we have repro, propose adding a telemetry flag to measure per-request ephemeral bytes for the next release so we can catch this in CI perf presubmit.

alex: +1. also add a perf regression alert on kernel_switch_count and kv_frag_ratio so future rollouts fail fast.

kevin: noted. saving logs to s3://redwood-perf/1977654321-gpu-rt-23-traces.tar.gz

maria: great. if anyone needs me I'll be on the perf call in 10.

kevin: thanks team. keeping thread updated. :thumbsup:
